[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Micro-frontend applications require testing at multiple levels: unit tests (component isolation), integration tests (cross-module interaction), E2E tests (full user workflows), accessibility tests (WCAG 2.2 AA), and contract tests (API boundaries). Traditional ASP.NET testing approaches (MSTest, Selenium) don't align with modern React testing practices (Vitest, React Testing Library, Playwright). Teams need comprehensive testing strategy covering all micro-frontend layers while maintaining fast feedback loops.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The Testing Strategy pattern defines multi-layer testing approach for micro-frontends: unit testing with Vitest and React Testing Library, integration testing across modules, E2E testing with Playwright, accessibility testing automation (axe-core, pa11y), contract testing for APIs, and PHI protection validation. The pattern includes CI/CD integration, performance budgets, and quality gates preventing regressions.

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

**Testing Reality:**

- Modern React testing requires different tools than ASP.NET
- Testing setup and ongoing execution represent a meaningful portion of development time
- Accessibility testing mandatory (Section 508/WCAG 2.2 AA)
- Must validate no PHI exposure in browser console, localStorage, analytics

**Current State (ASP.NET):**

- MSTest for unit/integration tests
- Selenium WebDriver for UI automation
- Manual accessibility testing (expensive, inconsistent)
- No contract testing between frontend/backend
- Long test execution times (10-30 minutes)

**Target State (React Micro-Frontends):**

- Vitest for unit tests (<1 second execution)
- React Testing Library for component tests
- Playwright for E2E tests (parallel execution)
- Automated accessibility testing (axe-core in CI/CD)
- Contract testing (Pact or MSW)
- Total test suite <5 minutes

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

**Testing Pyramid:**

```text
         /\
        /  \   E2E Tests (Slow, Expensive)
       /    \  - Playwright
      /------\ - 5-10% of tests
     /        \
    / Integration \ Integration Tests (Medium Speed)
   /    Tests      \ - 20-30% of tests
  /----------------\
 /  Unit Tests      \ Unit Tests (Fast, Cheap)
/____________________\ - 60-70% of tests
                       - Vitest + React Testing Library
```
page_texts.13:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

**Constraints:**

- **Test Execution Time**: Total test suite must complete in <5 minutes for CI/CD
- **Code Coverage Requirements**: 80% minimum coverage for unit tests
- **HIPAA Compliance**: No PHI in test data, console logs, or test artifacts
- **Accessibility Compliance**: WCAG 2.2 AA automated testing required
- **Developer Experience**: Tests must run fast locally (<1s unit tests)
- **CI/CD Budget**: Limit parallel E2E test runners (cost constraints)

**Competing Forces:**

- **Test Coverage vs Speed**: More tests = slower feedback loop
- **E2E Tests vs Maintenance**: E2E tests brittle, require frequent updates
- **Automated vs Manual Testing**: Automated catches 30-40% accessibility issues, manual testing still required
- **Test Isolation vs Integration**: Unit tests fast but don't catch integration bugs
- **Real Data vs Mocks**: Real APIs slow tests, mocks can drift from reality

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

Multi-layer testing strategy:

1. **Unit Tests (60-70%)**: Vitest + React Testing Library for component isolation
2. **Integration Tests (20-30%)**: Cross-module interaction via Module Federation
3. **E2E Tests (5-10%)**: Playwright for critical healthcare workflows
4. **Accessibility Tests**: axe-core automated testing in CI/CD
5. **Contract Tests**: API boundary validation (Pact or MSW)
6. **PHI Protection Tests**: Validate no PHI in console, localStorage, analytics

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Testing Strategy Layers                      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Layer 1: Unit Tests (Vitest + React Testing Library)
├── Component rendering tests
├── User interaction tests (click, type, submit)
├── State management tests (hooks, context)
├── Utility function tests
└── Execution: <1 second, runs on every file save

Layer 2: Integration Tests (Vitest + MSW)
├── API integration (mocked with MSW)
├── Cross-module communication
├── Authentication flows
├── Form validation and submission
└── Execution: 1-5 seconds, runs in CI/CD

Layer 3: E2E Tests (Playwright)
├── Critical user workflows (claims submission, eligibility check)
├── Cross-product navigation (Enterprise™ → Provider+™)
├── Multi-step processes (prior authorization workflow)
├── Error scenarios (validation failures, timeouts)
└── Execution: 2-5 minutes, runs in CI/CD (parallel)

Layer 4: Accessibility Tests (axe-core + pa11y)
├── Automated WCAG 2.2 AA validation
├── Keyboard navigation tests
├── Screen reader compatibility
├── Color contrast validation
└── Execution: 30 seconds, runs in CI/CD

Layer 5: Contract Tests (Pact or MSW)
├── API request/response validation
├── Breaking change detection
├── Versioned contract storage
└── Execution: 1-2 seconds, runs in CI/CD

Layer 6: PHI Protection Tests
├── Console log scanning (no PHI in console.log)
├── localStorage/sessionStorage validation (no PHI stored)
├── Analytics payload inspection (no PHI sent to GA/Datadog)
└── Execution: 5-10 seconds, runs in CI/CD
```

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

**Developer Test Workflow:**

1. **Local Development**:
   - Developer writes component code
   - Vitest watch mode runs unit tests automatically (<1s)
   - Developer sees immediate feedback
   - VS Code Test Explorer shows pass/fail

2. **Pre-Commit**:
   - Git hook runs `npm run test:unit`
   - All unit tests must pass before commit
   - Linter checks test file naming conventions
   - Commit blocked if tests fail

3. **Pull Request CI/CD**:
   - GitHub Actions triggers on PR
   - Parallel jobs: unit, integration, E2E, accessibility
   - Code coverage report posted as PR comment
   - Playwright test report uploaded as artifact
   - Merge blocked if any test fails

4. **Production Deployment**:
   - All tests pass in main branch
   - E2E smoke tests run against staging
   - Contract tests verify API compatibility
   - Deployment proceeds only if tests green

5. **Monitoring**:
   - Test execution time tracked (Datadog)
   - Flaky test detection (>5% failure rate)
   - Code coverage trend over time
   - Alert if coverage drops below 80%

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

**Variation 1: Vitest + React Testing Library** (Recommended)

- Fast unit tests (<1s)
- Great VS Code integration
- Modern ESM support
- Pros: Fastest feedback loop
- Cons: Newer tool, smaller ecosystem than Jest

**Variation 2: Jest + React Testing Library** (Legacy Projects)

- Mature ecosystem
- More plugins available
- Pros: Well-documented, battle-tested
- Cons: Slower than Vitest (3-5x), CJS configuration

**Variation 3: Cypress Component Testing** (Alternative)

- Component tests run in real browser
- Great debugging experience
- Pros: Real browser environment
- Cons: Slower than Vitest, requires Cypress infrastructure

**Variation 4: Contract Testing Approaches**

- **Pact**: Consumer-driven contracts, separate Pact Broker
- **MSW**: Mock Service Worker, simpler setup
- **Recommendation**: Start with MSW, migrate to Pact for multiple consumers

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#cicd-integration-github-actions]

#### CI/CD Integration (GitHub Actions)

```yaml
# .github/workflows/test.yml
name: Test

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run test:unit
      - run: npm run test:coverage
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3

  integration-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run test:integration

  e2e-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps
      - run: npm run test:e2e
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/

  accessibility-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run test:a11y
```

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- **Test User Behavior**: Test what users see, not implementation details
- **Avoid Test IDs**: Use accessible queries (getByRole, getByLabelText)
- **Fast Feedback**: Unit tests run on every file save (watch mode)
- **Flaky Test Zero Tolerance**: Fix flaky tests immediately or delete them
- **PHI Protection**: Never use real PHI in test data
- **Accessibility First**: Run axe-core on every page in E2E tests

### Real-World Example 1: Ohio MMIS Claims Search Testing

**Context:**
Ohio Enterprise™ MMIS claims search page with complex filtering, sorting, and pagination. Previously tested with Selenium (30-minute test execution). Needed to migrate to modern testing stack while improving coverage and speed.

**Implementation:**

1. **Unit Tests** (150 tests): Vitest + React Testing Library for component isolation
   - Filter logic tests (status, date range, amount)
   - Pagination component tests
   - Sort functionality tests
   - Execution time: 800ms total

2. **Integration Tests** (20 tests): MSW for API mocking
   - Claims API integration
   - Error handling (404, 500, timeout)
   - Loading states and skeleton screens
   - Execution time: 3 seconds total

3. **E2E Tests** (8 critical paths): Playwright parallel execution
   - Search by claim ID
   - Filter by multiple criteria
   - Export claims to CSV
   - Accessibility validation (axe-core)
   - Execution time: 2 minutes (parallel across 3 browsers)

4. **Accessibility Tests**: axe-core in Playwright
   - Keyboard navigation (Tab, Enter, Escape)
   - Screen reader labels (aria-labels)
   - Color contrast validation
   - Result: Zero violations found

**Outcome:**

- Test execution reduced from 30 minutes (Selenium) to 2.5 minutes (Vitest + Playwright)
- Code coverage increased from 45% to 87%
- Caught 12 accessibility violations before production
- Developer feedback: "Tests give me confidence to refactor"
- Zero production bugs in 3 months post-migration

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#real-world-example-2-provider-enrollment-form-testing]

### Real-World Example 2: Provider+™ Enrollment Form Testing

**Context:**
Provider enrollment form with 40+ fields, complex validation rules, document upload, and multi-step workflow. Previous testing approach: manual QA (2-3 days per release). Needed automated testing to enable weekly releases.

**Implementation:**

1. **Unit Tests** (200+ tests): Form field validation logic
   - Email format validation
   - NPI number validation
   - Tax ID validation
   - Phone number formatting
   - Date range validation (license expiration)

2. **Integration Tests** (30 tests): Form submission flows
   - Step-by-step navigation (Basic Info → Credentials → Documents)
   - Form state persistence (localStorage recovery)
   - File upload validation (size, type, virus scan)
   - API error handling

3. **E2E Tests** (15 tests): Complete enrollment workflows
   - Happy path (all fields valid)
   - Validation error scenarios
   - File upload and preview
   - Multi-browser testing (Chrome, Firefox, Safari)

4. **PHI Protection Tests**: Custom validation
   - Scan console logs for PHI patterns (SSN, DOB)
   - Verify no PHI in localStorage keys
   - Check analytics payloads (Datadog RUM)

**Outcome:**

- Automated testing reduced QA time from 2-3 days to 4 hours
- Enabled weekly releases (previously monthly)
- Caught PHI exposure bug in staging (console.log with provider SSN)
- Form submission success rate improved from 87% to 96% (better validation)
- Developer confidence in refactoring improved validation logic

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-015-testing-strategy-pattern.md#before-aspnet--selenium]

#### Before (ASP.NET + Selenium)

```text
Testing Stack:

- MSTest for unit tests
- Selenium WebDriver for UI automation
- Manual accessibility testing
- No contract testing
- No API mocking

Test Execution:

- Unit tests: 5 minutes (requires IIS, SQL Server)
- Selenium tests: 30 minutes (sequential execution)
- Total feedback loop: 35 minutes
- Flaky tests: 15-20% failure rate

Developer Experience:

- Run tests manually (not automated in IDE)
- Slow feedback (35-minute wait)
- Selenium tests brittle (ViewState changes break tests)
- No test coverage metrics
- Manual accessibility testing (2-3 days per release)

Quality Metrics:

- Code coverage: 40-50%
- Bug escape rate: 10-15% to production
- Accessibility issues: 20-30 per release (found manually)
```

#### After (Vitest + Playwright + axe-core)

```text
Testing Stack:

- Vitest + React Testing Library (unit/integration)
- Playwright (E2E testing, parallel execution)
- axe-core (automated accessibility)
- MSW (API mocking)
- Contract testing (Pact or MSW)

Test Execution:

- Unit tests: <1 second (watch mode)
- Integration tests: 3-5 seconds
- E2E tests: 2-5 minutes (parallel across browsers)
- Total feedback loop: <5 minutes
- Flaky tests: <5% (Playwright auto-retry)

Developer Experience:

- Tests run automatically on file save (Vitest watch)
- Fast feedback (<1s unit tests)
- VS Code Test Explorer integration
- Real-time code coverage display
- Automated accessibility testing in CI/CD

Quality Metrics:

- Code coverage: 80-90%
- Bug escape rate: <5% to production
- Accessibility issues: 5-10 per release (automated catches 30-40%)

Quantitative Improvements:
| Metric | Before (ASP.NET) | After (React) | Improvement |
|--------|------------------|---------------|-------------|
| Test Execution Time | 35 min | <5 min | 86% faster |
| Code Coverage | 45% | 87% | +93% |
| Flaky Test Rate | 15-20% | <5% | 70-75% reduction |
| Bug Escape Rate | 10-15% | <5% | 60-67% reduction |
| Accessibility Testing | Manual (2-3 days) | Automated (30s) | 99% faster |
| Developer Confidence | Low | High | Qualitative improvement |
```

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Micro-frontends require multi-layer testing (unit, integration, E2E, accessibility) with fast feedback loops.

**Solution:** Vitest + React Testing Library (unit), Playwright (E2E), axe-core (accessibility), MSW (API mocking), PHI protection validation in CI/CD.

**Key Benefits:**

- **Fast Feedback**: Unit tests <1 second
- **Comprehensive**: 60-70% unit, 20-30% integration, 5-10% E2E
- **Automated Accessibility**: Catch 30-40% of issues automatically

**Implementation Complexity:** **Medium** (4 weeks initial setup, ongoing test development)

**Related Patterns:** [ASP.NET Migration](./PTN-APP-MFE-013-pattern.md) | [Design System](./PTN-APP-MFE-005-pattern.md)
